## Norm Inequalities for Operator Monotone, Concave, and Convex Functions

A significant line of research in matrix analysis concerns norm inequalities that relate the values of a function evaluated at individual matrices to its value at their sum. In foundational work, Ando and Zhan established a family of such inequalities connecting $f(A) + f(B)$ to $f(A+B)$ for operator monotone functions $f$. These results captured a subtle interplay between the spectral behaviour of positive semidefinite matrices and the analytic properties of the functions applied to them. Subsequently, the scope of these inequalities was broadened considerably: Bourin and Uchiyama, along with Kosem, extended the Ando–Zhan framework beyond operator monotone functions to the larger classes of concave and convex functions, thereby revealing that the essential phenomena persist under weaker structural assumptions.

## Motivation and Central Question

Closely related to the results above is another set of inequalities due to Ando, which involve functions evaluated at the absolute difference of two matrices—namely, expressions of the form $f(|A-B|)$ and $g(|A-B|)$. Given the successful generalisation of the sum-type inequalities from operator monotone functions to concave and convex functions, it is natural to ask whether an analogous extension is possible in this difference-based setting. Specifically, this paper investigates whether Ando's inequalities involving $f(|A-B|)$ and $g(|A-B|)$ can be extended to the broader classes of non-negative concave functions $f$ and convex functions $g$.

## Main Results

The investigation yields both negative and positive conclusions, delineating precisely the boundaries within which such a generalisation can hold.

On the negative side, the authors demonstrate that the desired extension fails for general matrices. By exhibiting suitable counterexamples, they show that the passage from operator monotone functions to arbitrary non-negative concave and convex functions does not preserve the inequalities in full generality. This provides a definitive negative answer to the central question when no additional constraints are imposed on the matrices involved.

On the positive side, the situation improves markedly under an appropriate spectral hypothesis. The authors prove that the generalisation does hold in the special case where $A \ge \|B\|$—that is, when the matrix $A$ dominates the norm of $B$ in the positive semidefinite order. Under this condition, the inequalities extend affirmatively to non-negative concave and convex functions, thereby identifying a natural and meaningful regime in which the analogy with the sum-type results remains valid.

## A New Tool: $Y$-Dominated Majorisation

Beyond resolving the motivating question, the paper contributes a conceptual innovation of independent interest. The authors introduce the notion of *$Y$-dominated majorisation*, a refined relation between the spectra of two Hermitian matrices. This concept enriches the classical theory of majorisation by incorporating an additional matrix parameter $Y$ that governs the comparison of eigenvalue sequences.

Using this new framework, the authors are able to sharpen the existing results of Bourin–Uchiyama and Kosem. The strengthened inequalities obtained through $Y$-dominated majorisation not only recover the earlier statements but also provide more precise information about the relationship between the spectra involved. In this way, the paper both clarifies the limits of one natural generalisation and advances the underlying theory with a versatile new tool.

# Generalizations of Ando's Norm Inequalities for Concave and Convex Functions

## Introduction and Background

A central theme in matrix analysis concerns the behavior of scalar functions when applied to matrices, and in particular how the resulting matrix functions respond to perturbations of their arguments. Among the most elegant results in this direction are the norm inequalities associated with the names of Ando, Zhan, Bourin, Uchiyama, and Kosem. These inequalities quantify the extent to which the map $A \mapsto f(A)$ is continuous or Lipschitz-like with respect to unitarily invariant norms, and they have found wide application throughout operator theory, quantum information, and the perturbation theory of eigenvalues.

The starting point of the present work is a pair of classical inequalities due to Ando. For an operator monotone function $f$ on the nonnegative half-line and Hermitian matrices $A, B$, one has the norm bound
$$
|||f(A) - f(B)||| \le |||f(|A - B|)|||,
$$
valid for every unitarily invariant norm $|||\cdot|||$. There is a natural convex counterpart to this statement, in which the direction of the inequality is reversed for an appropriate class of convex functions. Together these two results give sharp control on the difference $f(A) - f(B)$ in terms of the difference of the arguments $|A - B|$, and they encode deep structural information about operator monotone and operator convex functions.

## The Question of Generalization

In recent years, a program of research has sought to relax the strong hypotheses required by such inequalities. In particular, several extensions of the related Ando–Zhan inequalities have been obtained in which the operator monotone (respectively operator convex) hypothesis is weakened to mere concavity (respectively convexity) of the scalar function. These extensions raise a natural and compelling question: do Ando's inequalities themselves admit the same broadening?

Concretely, the paper investigates whether the bound
$$
|||f(A) - f(B)||| \le |||f(|A - B|)|||
$$
continues to hold when $f$ is only assumed to be a nonnegative concave function, and whether the dual inequality survives when $g$ is merely convex, rather than requiring the much more restrictive operator monotone or operator convex properties. Because concavity is a strictly weaker condition than operator monotonicity, an affirmative answer would substantially enlarge the scope of Ando's theory and align it with the recent progress on the Ando–Zhan side.

## Main Results

The authors establish that the answer is subtle and depends critically on the relationship between the two matrices involved. Their findings can be summarized in two complementary parts.

**Failure in the general case.** For arbitrary Hermitian (or positive semidefinite) matrices $A$ and $B$, the proposed generalizations do *not* hold. The authors construct explicit counterexamples showing that, once one departs from operator monotone functions to the broader class of nonnegative concave functions, the inequality $|||f(A) - f(B)||| \le |||f(|A - B|)|||$ can fail, and similarly the convex counterpart breaks down for general convex $g$. This demonstrates a genuine obstruction: the passage from operator monotonicity to ordinary concavity cannot be made without additional structural assumptions, in contrast to what one might have hoped by analogy with the Ando–Zhan setting.

**Validity under a separation hypothesis.** Despite this negative result, the authors identify a natural and clean condition under which the generalizations do hold. Specifically, when the matrices satisfy the ordering condition
$$
A \ge \|B\|,
$$
that is, when $A$ dominates $B$ in the sense that the smallest eigenvalue of $A$ is at least the operator norm (largest eigenvalue) of $B$, the desired inequalities are recovered for nonnegative concave $f$ and, dually, for convex $g$. This separation hypothesis effectively guarantees that the spectra of $A$ and $B$ are arranged so that the concavity of $f$ can be exploited in a controlled manner, restoring the good behavior familiar from the operator monotone theory.

## A New Notion: $Y$-Dominated Majorisation

A significant methodological contribution of the paper is the introduction of a new concept, which the authors call **$Y$-dominated majorisation**. Majorisation—the comparison of the ordered eigenvalue or singular value sequences of two matrices—is the natural language in which unitarily invariant norm inequalities are expressed, since a majorisation relation implies the corresponding family of norm inequalities. The refinement developed here strengthens the classical majorisation relations by incorporating an auxiliary operator $Y$ that constrains and sharpens the comparison.

Using this tool, the authors are able to prove results that are strictly stronger than several previously known theorems. In particular, their $Y$-dominated majorisation refines and unifies earlier results of Bourin and Uchiyama, as well as those of Kosem, on the subadditivity and related norm inequalities for concave functions of positive operators. The new framework thus not only yields the specific generalizations of Ando's inequalities under the separation hypothesis, but also provides a versatile mechanism that improves upon the existing landscape of concave function inequalities.

## Conclusion

Taken together, the results delineate precisely the boundary between what is and is not possible in extending Ando's norm inequalities beyond the operator monotone setting. The general failure of the inequalities cautions against overly optimistic analogies with the Ando–Zhan theory, while the positive result under $A \ge \|B\|$ isolates a meaningful regime in which the theory persists. Perhaps most importantly, the notion of $Y$-dominated majorisation emerges as a tool of independent interest, capable of strengthening a range of established results and likely to find further applications in the study of matrix and operator inequalities.

# Abstract

Let $A, B$ be positive semidefinite matrices and let $f: [0, \infty) \to [0, \infty)$ be a continuous function. We investigate norm inequalities relating $f(A+B)$ to $f(A) + f(B)$ for the class of concave functions, and dually for convex functions vanishing at the origin. Extending a result of Bourin and Uchiyama, and a related inequality of Kosem, we establish that for every symmetric (unitarily invariant) norm $\|\cdot\|$ and every nonnegative concave function $f$,
$$
\|f(A+B)\| \leq \|f(A) + f(B)\|,
$$
while the reverse inequality holds whenever $f$ is nonnegative convex with $f(0) = 0$. Our approach unifies and sharpens earlier arguments, replacing the majorization techniques of Ando and Zhan with a more flexible interpolation scheme based on integral representations of operator concave functions. As a consequence, we obtain several refinements involving the trace and the operator norm, and we recover the classical subadditivity results of Ando for the special case $f(t) = t^{p}$ with $0 < p \leq 1$.

We further extend these inequalities to the setting of $n$-tuples of positive semidefinite matrices, proving that
$$
\Big\| f\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{n} A_i\Big) \Big\| \leq \Big\| \sum_{i=1}^{n} f(A_i) \Big\|
$$
for all concave $f \geq 0$, and we discuss the sharpness of the constants involved. Counterexamples are provided to show that the corresponding operator inequalities in the Löwner order generally fail, thereby delineating the precise scope within which the norm estimates remain valid. We conclude with applications to entropy inequalities and to perturbation bounds for matrix means.

---

*Keywords:* unitarily invariant norms, concave and convex functions, positive semidefinite matrices, subadditivity, majorization, operator inequalities.

*2020 Mathematics Subject Classification:* 15A60, 47A30, 15A42, 47A63.

# Abstract

**On Unitarily Invariant Norm Inequalities for Operator Functions via Dominated Majorisation**

We investigate a class of unitarily invariant norm inequalities of the form
$$|||f(A) - f(B)||| \leq |||f(|A - B|)|||$$
for positive semidefinite matrices $A, B$ and functions $f$ belonging to suitable classes. Such inequalities constitute a natural refinement of classical perturbation bounds and connect the analytic properties of $f$ with the spectral geometry of operator differences.

The foundational results in this direction are due to Ando and Zhan, who established that the above inequality holds for every unitarily invariant norm whenever $f$ is a nonnegative operator monotone function on $[0, \infty)$, and dually, that the reverse-type inequality $|||f(A) + f(B)||| \leq |||f(A + B)|||$ holds for nonnegative operator convex functions with $f(0) = 0$. These theorems, resting on the theory of doubly substochastic maps and integral representations of operator monotone functions, have become cornerstones of matrix perturbation theory and have stimulated substantial subsequent work by Bhatia, Kittaneh, and others.

In this paper we introduce the notion of **dominated majorisation**, a strengthening of weak majorisation in which the majorising sequence is controlled pointwise by a monotone envelope derived from $f$. We show that dominated majorisation provides a unifying framework from which both the Ando–Zhan inequalities and several of their known refinements can be recovered, while simultaneously extending their scope to broader classes of concave and operator convex functions that need not be operator monotone. Our principal result establishes that dominated majorisation between the singular value sequences of $f(A) - f(B)$ and $f(|A - B|)$ is equivalent to a family of trace inequalities indexed by symmetric gauge functions, thereby characterising precisely when the norm inequality persists.

As applications, we derive new bounds for Hölder-type functions $f(t) = t^r$ with $0 < r \leq 1$, sharpen existing commutator estimates, and obtain stability results for operator means. We further discuss the failure of these inequalities in the operator norm setting for $r > 1$ and provide counterexamples delineating the boundary of validity. The dominated majorisation approach clarifies the role played by operator convexity versus ordinary convexity and suggests several open problems concerning multivariable extensions and non-Hermitian generalisations.

**Keywords:** unitarily invariant norms, operator monotone functions, majorisation, Ando–Zhan inequality, singular values, matrix perturbation theory

**MSC 2020:** 15A60, 47A30, 15A42, 47A63

# Abstract

## Generalizing Ando's Operator Inequalities to Concave and Convex Functions

We investigate the extent to which Ando's classical operator inequalities can be generalized to arbitrary operator concave and operator convex functions. Ando's foundational results established key monotonicity and convexity properties for specific operator functions, and a natural question concerns whether these inequalities persist across the broader classes of operator concave and convex functions.

In this work, we demonstrate that such generalizations fail in the general setting. Specifically, we construct explicit counterexamples showing that the proposed inequalities do not hold for arbitrary pairs of self-adjoint matrices, even when the functions involved satisfy the requisite operator concavity or convexity conditions. These counterexamples clarify the essential limitations inherent in extending Ando-type results without additional structural hypotheses.

Motivated by these obstructions, we identify a sufficient condition under which the desired inequalities are recovered. We prove that when the operators satisfy the ordering condition **A ≥ ‖B‖**, the generalized inequalities hold for all operator concave (respectively, operator convex) functions. Under this hypothesis, we establish positive results that faithfully extend Ando's original framework, providing both the correct direction of the inequalities and rigorous proofs based on integral representations and standard majorization techniques.

Our findings delineate a sharp boundary between the failure of these inequalities in full generality and their validity under the norm-domination condition, thereby refining the understanding of operator monotone and operator convex function theory in the context of Ando's inequalities.

**Keywords:** operator inequalities, operator concave functions, operator convex functions, Ando's inequality, self-adjoint operators, matrix analysis
